Uses of NSAIDs

  • Used in inflammation and for pain
  • May be used for mild antipyretic effect
  • Has been used to inhibit polyp formation in familial adenomatous polyposis
  • Long term use reduce the risk of colon cancer through unknown mechanism

Mechanism of Action

  • NSAIDs have anti-inflammatory activity that is chiefly mediated by inhibition of prostaglandin biosynthesis
  • There is non selective NSAIDs and those work by inhibiting COX 1 and COX 2 and there is new agents which are selective for inhibiting COX 2 only

Cyclooxygenase 1 and 2

  • COX 1 regulates normal cellular processes, such as gastric cytoprotection, vascular homeostasis, platelets aggregation, and reproductive and kidney functions
  • COX 2 expressed in tissues such as the brain , kidney and bone. It is expression at other sites is increased during states of chronic inflammation
  • Inhibition of COX 2 is thought to lead to the anti inflammatory and analgesic action of NSAIDs while inhibition of COX 1 leads to most of the side effects

Selective NSAIDs

  • So they synthesized COX 2 selective NSAIDs which had the same efficacy to reduce pain and inflammation as it for the non selective NSAIDs and had improved GIT safety and reduced risk of bleeding
  • But these drugs had increased in incidence of edema, hypertension and possibly myocardial infarction which made their use limited

Examples

  • Non selective
  • Aspirin
  • Diclofenac
  • Ibuprofen
  • Naproxen
  • Mefenamic acid
  • Indomethacin
  • Ketoprofen
  • Piroxicam
  • Selective
  • Celecoxib
  • Meloxicam

Adverse Effects

  • Gastrointestinal
  • Increased risk of bleeding
  • Actions on the kidney
  • Cardiac effects
  • Drug interactions
  • Toxicity
